blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.text: Abstract

blocks.en: A mathematical framework that predicts crop stress, estimates protectant demand, and evaluates the feasibility of deploying ReLEAF across Taiwan.
blocks.text: A mathematical framework that predicts crop stress, estimates protectant demand, and evaluates the feasibility of deploying ReLEAF across Taiwan.

blocks.en: To evaluate ReLEAF's effectiveness and scalability, we developed mathematical models using historical agricultural records, weather data, and experimental measurements. Incorporating weather variables into 25 years of rice yield data reduced prediction error by 32% compared to the baseline trend model. We also modeled protectant activity, treatment timing, dosage, and production capacity to estimate the resources needed under different stress conditions. Finally, we evaluated the potential costs of deploying ReLEAF across Taiwan's 346 farming townships, connecting laboratory findings with real-world agricultural applications.

We also modeled protectant activity, treatment timing, dosage, and production capacity to estimate the resources needed under different stress conditions. Finally, we evaluated the potential costs of deploying ReLEAF across Taiwan's 346 farming townships, connecting laboratory findings with real-world agricultural applications.

blocks.en: Timing constraints on delivery
blocks.text: Timing constraints on delivery

blocks.en: ReLEAF's reactor makes a protectant (throughout this page the protectant is modeled from our wet lab data on one of the protectants we engineered and produced, ACC deaminase) only while its green lamp is on, so the model has to set the light level and its duration. Sizing the system by volume, the liters of culture one hectare requires, gives an unstable answer: that figure depends on a dose we have not minimized and a canopy correction we have not measured.

blocks.en: Timing is the better-posed problem, because three independent intervals have to fit inside one window. A weather forecast extends about three days. The reactor takes days to fill. The plant requires the protectant at a particular time relative to the stress, and that time is still contested at the bench.

blocks.en: The three intervals do not fit. One hectare's application takes 5.4 days on ten 20-liter units against a three-day forecast, so 2.4 days of production precede any forecast that would justify it. That is the co-treatment case, with the protectant arriving as the stress lands. If the agar result in M3 stands and the protectant has to be on the plant one day earlier, production starts 6.4 days ahead and 3.4 of those days precede the forecast. The reactor therefore cannot be scheduled from the forecast. It produces through the season and the forecast determines when stock is used, which makes the shelf life of that stock the controlling quantity on this page. M2 contains the only readings that bear on it, and they do not agree on the direction.

blocks.en: Stress index from the harvest record
blocks.text: Stress index from the harvest record

blocks.en: Most crop stress indices weight temperature, water and light by expert judgment. Here the weights are fitted to Taiwan's harvest record instead. Taiwan grows two rice crops a year in the same field: the first crop (一期) is transplanted around February and harvested in June, the second crop (二期) in July and November. The two meet different weather, so they are fitted separately, and an index value is always quoted with its crop.

The two meet different weather, so they are fitted separately, and an index value is always quoted with its crop.

blocks.en: A season whose yield fell below its county trend was a stressed season. For each crop we fitted all 2<sup>15</sup> − 1 = 32 767 combinations of fifteen candidate stresses and scored every one on years it had not seen. The second crop pays for wind, light and badly timed water. Heat adds nothing once those three are included, which matters because the wet lab runs a heat program this index does not support.

blocks.en: The case for precision came from natural farmers. Ms. Chen and Dr. Li (seen in IHP page), who farm in northwest Taiwan, maintain that raising a crop is like raising a child: a plant protected from every stress never builds the tolerance it would otherwise have. That sets the specification this index is built to. The reactor should produce only when a threshold that accurately reflects crop condition is crossed, so the 32% error reduction in the second crop is evidence for a release rule that initiates for the right reason. The index decides only whether to act; its demand level sets the light intensity in M2, and the amount that reaches the crop is settled in M4.

blocks.en: The first crop is the weaker of the two fits and it is the one now being tested blind: the 2026 first-crop forecast was frozen on September 26, before any county published, and four of sixteen counties have reported, at 7.9% county error against the trend's 8.8%. Four counties are too few to establish prospective performance. The model underpredicted Hualien and Pingtung and overpredicted Taitung; only Taichung fell close to its prediction. The second crop is not harvested until November, so the better-fitting of the two models has not yet been tested blind.

blocks.en: Induction and activity in culture
blocks.text: Induction and activity in culture

blocks.en: The reactor contains Bacillus subtilis WB800 carrying the cyanobacterial CcaSR system. Green light at 535 nm activates CcaS, CcaR~P drives PcpcG2, and the protectant gene behind a secretion signal puts active enzyme in the supernatant. The intensity that gives a target output comes from the Hill function Castillo-Hair et al. (2019) fitted in B. subtilis, inverted; both appear in the Equations section. Nothing we have run tests that curve, because every induction so far has been at one setting.

blocks.en: One tube was held at 3850 lux of green and sampled twice, at three hours of induction and again at six. The assay signal did not accumulate between those samples. It fell, from 0.5503 mM of α-ketobutyrate to 0.1414, or 26% of the three-hour value. Read as first-order loss through two points, that is an apparent half-time of 1.5 hours.

blocks.en: Two limits apply to that figure. The tube was still producing enzyme across the interval, so the decline is net and the underlying decay is at least this fast. And it is live, illuminated cells in their own medium, not a harvested preparation.

blocks.en: A second reading of the same sample agrees. The DNPH reaction on that sample ran 28 hours; averaged over that period the activity is 0.33 mU mL⁻¹, 22 times below the 7.25 mU mL⁻¹ an earlier supernatant assay reported over 30 minutes. The measured product corresponds to 1.3% of the initial 43 mM ACC, assuming both concentrations are on the same reaction-volume basis, so bulk substrate depletion does not account for the low average rate. A single decay with a time constant of 1.0 hours passes through both readings. That is a half-life of 0.7 hours, and it puts the initial rate at 9.2 mU mL⁻¹, the same order as the earlier assay.

blocks.en: Read in the culture and in the assay tube, that one sample puts the apparent lifetime of the secreted protectant between 0.7 and 1.5 hours. A later run does not reproduce the fall. After twelve hours of dark instead of sixteen, the culture was sampled in triplicate at three, six and eight hours of illumination, and activity rose across the series, from 8.3 to 18.1 nmol α-ketobutyrate mL⁻¹ h⁻¹ against a pre-illumination baseline of 2.8. The tube that fell was read once; the run that rose is the replicated one. Together they put the timescale at hours and leave the sign of the change open.

blocks.en: Since July the plant team has run one design: the protectant is applied one day before the salt, with it, or one day after. The design answers whether a farm needs a prediction at all. If pre-treatment is better, ReLEAF requires a forecast; if co-treatment is better, it requires a full tank and a fast response, which is a different system. Three runs have reported and they disagree.

blocks.en: The activity term cancels out of the capital result. The dose is a volume of our own culture and the reactor's output is that same culture per day, so the secreted activity appears once in the numerator and once in the denominator of the vessel calculation. At 0.5 mU/mL or at 7.25, the two ends of our own DNPH readings, the answer is the same 81 L per hectare, and everything below the vessel line follows: the fleet, the capital and the payback do not depend on which reading is finally adopted. The activity figure sets the protectant tally in kU and the mass in grams, and whether the dose works at all, which no run of ours bounds.

blocks.en: What the capital does depend on is the harvest cycle. The throughput row is a concentration over a batch cycle of five hours, or 4.8 harvests a day, and a 72-hour reactor run read by anti-His ELISA does not support that: the concentration peaks at 12 h, holds its band of 2.5 to 6.5 µg/mL to 30 h, then falls to about half from 36 h on. DNPH on the same supernatants peaks six hours later, at 18 h. A 12-hour cycle puts the vessel at 195 L per hectare and the capital at US$9120; an 18-hour cycle puts them at 292 L and US$13 679. The ledger keeps five hours, which is what the throughput was measured against, and keeps the range as a limit.

blocks.en: Two rows come with a caveat. The canopy correction is modeled from a leaf area index of 4.5 against 0.115 on a seedling plate and spans 1.68 to 3.52, so the 5188 L is a scenario and not a validated rice dose. The experiment that produced 1.67 mL varied salt level and timing but not the applied amount, so 2126 L/ha is the dose that worked and the smallest that works is unknown. A single plate with neat, 1:3, 1:10 and 1:30 arms would locate the minimum, and every row below it would move.

blocks.en: Payback and fleet utilization
blocks.text: Payback and fleet utilization

blocks.en: Ten units cost US$9375. The stress index attributes US$138 per hectare per crop of loss on an ordinary Yunlin (雲林) paddy to the weather this protectant acts on. Under the current trigger only the second crop generates application windows, so one crop a year returns anything. Efficacy is the share of that loss the protectant recovers; no run of ours bounds it, so payback is plotted across the whole axis.

Under the current trigger only the second crop generates application windows, so one crop a year returns anything. Efficacy is the share of that loss the protectant recovers; no run of ours bounds it, so payback is plotted across the whole axis.

blocks.en: No point on that axis returns the capital on a useful horizon. At efficacy 1 the payback is 68 years, and five years would require an efficacy of 14, which exceeds the loss itself. Geospatial Analysis reaches a different figure from its own chlorophyll work: a net benefit of US$1931 per hectare per crop, paying back in 4.9 years, which is 14 times the whole loss this index attributes to weather. The two rest on different stress definitions and different biological assumptions, so they are not yet two estimates of the same hectare. Section 5 sets out what would settle it.

blocks.en: The second constraint is utilization. Only the second crop generates windows, and within it 17 of 25 seasons never cross the threshold. A qualifying season needs 9 passes, the median across the seasons that qualify on a provisional trigger and an assumed two-day protection window, at 5.4 days each, or 49 reactor-days inside a crop of about 120 days, so one ten-unit fleet covers 2.5 hectares and operates on 4.3% of the calendar.

blocks.en: Payback therefore depends on ownership. One fleet shared across the 2.5 hectares it can serve divides the capital accordingly: 27 years on this page's loss figure at efficacy 1, and 2.0 years on the Geospatial Analysis figure. On either benefit estimate, a reactor owned by a single farm is idle for most of its service life.

blocks.en: Geospatial Analysis answers a similar but distinct question. It derives units per hectare from soil class, which governs how far and how long the protectant remains where it is applied; this page derives units per hectare from reactor throughput, which governs whether enough can be made at all. A deployment has to satisfy both constraints, and the binding one will differ by township, so the two densities need reconciling before either is quoted as the number of machines a field requires.

blocks.en: The two pages also disagree on the benefit, by the factor of 14 set out in M5. Either this index misses most of what stress costs a field, or the chlorophyll-to-yield step in Geospatial Analysis is too generous. Three measurements would settle it: a yield endpoint in place of a chlorophyll one, a single stress definition across both pages, and agreement on whether a protected hectare returns once or twice a year.

blocks.en: They agree on ownership by different routes. Geospatial Analysis puts capital per hectare at or above a full year of gross paddy revenue in every soil class; this page reaches the same place from utilization, since a machine that stands idle for most of its service life cannot be bought by the farm it serves. With 99% of Taiwanese farmers working under two hectares, a shared asset held by a farmers' association is the only structure the arithmetic permits. Two costs a farmer pays are absent from this ledger: refill cartridges and hardware service life. The straw-return mechanism in the business plan acts on the first.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.text: Conclusion

blocks.en: The model was built to size a dose and the binding result is the size of the equipment. Taiwan's harvest record supplies a stress index that gives 32% less county error than the no-weather trend in the second crop, and a frozen 2026 forecast is now being scored against the harvest. From there the chain is a few steps of arithmetic over one modeled correction: 37.6 kU of protectant per hectare, 81 liters of vessel to make it in a season, and US$3800 of capital to buy them.
blocks.text: The model was built to size a dose and the binding result is the size of the equipment. Taiwan's harvest record supplies a stress index that gives 32% less county error than the no-weather trend in the second crop, and a frozen 2026 forecast is now being scored against the harvest. From there the chain is a few steps of arithmetic over one modeled correction: 37.6 kU of protectant per hectare, 81 liters of vessel to make it in a season, and US$3800 of capital to buy them.

blocks.en: Two results constrain the system as specified. It takes 5.4 days to serve one hectare against a three-day forecast, so it has to operate on banked stock; and it covers 2.5 hectares while operating on 4.3% of the calendar, which puts individual ownership out of reach at the farm size 99% of Taiwanese farmers work. Geospatial Analysis reaches the same conclusion from soil and revenue rather than throughput.
blocks.text: Two results constrain the system as specified. It takes 5.4 days to serve one hectare against a three-day forecast, so it has to operate on banked stock; and it covers 2.5 hectares while operating on 4.3% of the calendar, which puts individual ownership out of reach at the farm size 99% of Taiwanese farmers work. Geospatial Analysis reaches the same conclusion from soil and revenue rather than throughput.

blocks.en: Two results are unresolved. Activity in the culture moves on a timescale of hours, but not in a settled direction: one tube fell to an apparent half-time of 0.7 to 1.5 hours, and a replicated run rose over its first eight hours of light. Neither measures a harvested preparation, which is what a banking plan turns on. And the benefit a protected hectare returns is in dispute by a factor of 14 between this page and Geospatial Analysis. Neither gap closes with further modeling. Both close at a bench, and Current limits names the experiments.

blocks.en: Current limits
blocks.text: Current limits

blocks.en: Eight things this model cannot yet do. Efficacy is unbounded: no plant run of ours constrains how much of a salinity loss the protectant takes back, so every figure in dollars is drawn against efficacy and never at a value. The dose is one that worked, not the smallest that works, and no dilution series has been run. The canopy correction is modeled and spans 1.68 to 3.52, and every row of the ledger below it inherits that. The concentration rests on a single supernatant assay below the quantitation limit, and the 28-hour endpoint that would check it cannot be distinguished from a stalled reaction. The harvest cycle of five hours behind the throughput row is the one bench number the capital result depends on, since the activity term cancels; a 72-hour ELISA run puts the concentration peak at 12 h and a halving after 30 h, which a five-hour cycle does not obviously fit, and at 12 or 18 hours the capital is US$9120 or US$13 679 a hectare instead of US$3800. Shelf life has no direct measurement. The figure standing in for it, an apparent half-time of 0.7 to 1.5 hours by two routes, comes from one unreplicated tube read in live culture while the cells were still producing; a replicated run rose over its first eight hours of light. Both bound activity in the vessel; neither reaches the lifetime of a harvested preparation, which is what the banked-stock plan turns on, and whether a concentrated, cooled or formulated stock lasts longer is untested. The protection window is assumed at two days per pass, which is what fixes a firing season at nine passes. The release rule is counted from waterlogging while the payback is priced on salinity; making them agree means rebuilding the rule around salt-sensitive growth stages. That would need roughly fifteen applications in a 30-day window instead of nine, or 81 reactor-days inside 30, which the current fleet could not serve for one hectare without banking far in advance.

Shelf life has no direct measurement. The figure standing in for it, an apparent half-time of 0.7 to 1.5 hours by two routes, comes from one unreplicated tube read in live culture while the cells were still producing; a replicated run rose over its first eight hours of light. Both bound activity in the vessel; neither reaches the lifetime of a harvested preparation, which is what the banked-stock plan turns on, and whether a concentrated, cooled or formulated stock lasts longer is untested. The protection window is assumed at two days per pass, which is what fixes a firing season at nine passes. The release rule is counted from waterlogging while the payback is priced on salinity; making them agree means rebuilding the rule around salt-sensitive growth stages. That would need roughly fifteen applications in a 30-day window instead of nine, or 81 reactor-days inside 30, which the current fleet could not serve for one hectare without banking far in advance.
